cf_flaky.mutated_regex: return x \*\* 2|return x \+ 2|return x << 1|return 2 \* x|return x \* 2 \*\* 1
cf_flaky.why: double(2) is 4 for these operators; the only other covering test fails at random whatever the code does

cf_flaky.mutated_regex: return x \* 3|return x \* 1|return x - 2|return x / 2|return None

cf_import_time.why: TABLE is built at import time; lookup(3) == 6 sees the mutated table (killed, never 'no coverage')

cf_session_fixture.why: a session fixture computed once per process still reads the mutated value in a fresh process

cf_subprocess.why: the CLI runs in a child interpreter that imports the mutated file from disk
the child prints something other than 'many'

cf_infinite_loop.why: the loop never ends: a hang is a kill (a timeout verdict detects it), and the campaign must not hang

cf_unicode.mutated_regex: if not name|if name is None

cf_unicode.why: shout('abc') or shout('ab') changes; the edit lies after non-ASCII text on its line

cf_cached.why: the first test caches the mutated rate, the second asserts the price computed from it

cf_hard_exit.why: checked(5) reaches os._exit: the worker dies, which is a kill

cf_cov_config.why: double(2) == 4 holds for 2 * 2 and 2 ** 2; the project's pytest configuration runs pytest-cov (--cov)

cf_decorator_closure.why: successor is decorated at import time: the wrapper in its closure is the mutated one, and successor(1) == 2 fails
1 << 1 is 2 as well: the only test cannot tell the mutant from the original

cf_init_target.why: the mutated file is the package's __init__.py; greet('there') == 'hello there' fails

cf_nested_class.why: Grid defines the nested class Cell; Grid(3).area() == 9 holds only for the original product

cf_pool.why: triple(2) == 6 fails; the suite also has a test that starts a multiprocessing.Pool

cf_property_setter.why: the getter shares the qualified name Thermostat.target with the setter; target reads 25 after setting 25
the setter caps at 30: 25 stays 25 and 40 becomes 30
the name-mangled method __floor raises 5 to 10 through set_safe
min is symmetric: the swapped arguments are an equivalent mutant
max is symmetric: the swapped arguments are an equivalent mutant

cf_relative_import.why: the only test is a square (2, 2): 2 + 2 and 2 ** 2 are 4 as well
area(2, 2) == 4 fails; the module imports SCALE relatively, and the project turns warnings into errors

cf_src_pythonpath.why: the test imports its helper through pytest.ini's pythonpath = src tests; total([3, 4]) == 8 fails

cf_tabs.why: the file is indented with tabs; add(2) == 2 and add(3) == 5 fail
